21-half-clutch: Is your left foot quietly eating your clutch?
Resting your foot on the pedal, or holding the car on a slope with half clutch, keeps the clutch plate slipping.
Slipping means friction and heat. The plate and the release bearing wear out much faster.
And a clutch job costs a lot more than you think.
The fix: foot off the pedal while driving, handbrake on slopes, and press the clutch fully when you shift.

22-engine-oil: Your car barely moved this year. Does it still need an oil change?
Yes. Oil ages by kilometres and by time. Even parked, it oxidises and picks up moisture.
Follow your owner's manual: change it at the set kilometres or every twelve months, whichever comes first.
City stop-go traffic is severe use, so change it on the earlier side.
And check the dipstick once a month.

23-alignment-vs-balancing: Steering vibrates at eighty? It's probably not alignment.
Balancing fixes uneven weight on the wheel. The sign is vibration in the steering or seat at speed.
Alignment fixes the wheel angles. The signs are the car pulling to one side, an off-centre steering wheel, or a tyre worn on one edge.
Get both checked after a big pothole hit, with new tyres, or every five to ten thousand kilometres.
Save this for your next service.
24-brake-pads: Your brakes warn you before they fail. Are you listening?
A high-pitched squeal when you brake is the wear indicator touching the disc.
Grinding means the pad is finished and metal is hitting metal. Now the disc gets damaged too.
Longer stopping distance, or a soft pedal, is another warning.
So is a brake warning light, or the car pulling to one side when you brake.
Any of these? Get it checked this week.
25-level2-adas: Your car has ADAS. So can it drive itself? No.
Level two means the car helps with steering and speed together: adaptive cruise plus lane keep assist.
But your hands stay on the wheel and your eyes stay on the road, always.
Faded lane lines, bikes cutting in and busy Indian traffic can confuse it.
Use it as a helper on highways, not as a driver.

26-sunroof: Everyone wants a sunroof. Should you pay for one?
The good part: the cabin feels airy and the car looks premium.
The catch: Indian summers can heat up the cabin, it adds cost and weight, and the drain channels need cleaning to avoid leaks.
And never stand out of the sunroof while driving. It's dangerous, and you can be fined.
Worth it only if you'll really use it on cool evenings and highway drives.
